rationale: Region = the two observed encoder stage bundles model.resnet.encoder.stages.0 (call ed609fcfe9f1b7538a7256aa) and stages.1 (call e4174ed71f25bb1aa98a4321), which share group 928c554228ed389eec5f, plus every computational group fully contained in their subtrees. The accepted revision (current parent, chunked-stem candidate, paired-measured peak_allocated_bytes 204,905,472 vs original 281,975,808) moved the allocator peak out of the stem and into stages.0: during stages.0.layers.1 the live set is weights 46,758,048 + GPU-resident pixels 19,267,584 + stem output 25,690,112 (encoder-loop reference) + layers.0 output 25,690,112 (stage-loop reference) + up to three more 25,690,112 B (32,64,56,56) temporaries inside conv2->batch_norm->relu = 194.5 MB of live tensors plus ~10 MB conv workspace/aux, matching the observed 204.9 MB; all later activations are <= 12.85 MB per tensor. The secondary moment is stages.1.layers.0 (transition 64->128 s2 with 1x1 shortcut): pixels+weights+25.69 MB input + up to five 12,845,056 B (32,128,28,28) temporaries ~ 143 MB, which would become the new peak if only stages.0 were edited, so both stage calls in the shared group are selected as one joint region. The replacement mirrors the accepted stem pattern: module-boundary direct-callable replacements at the two stage boundaries that stream the frozen batch through the identical parent aten operators (conv2d, eval batch_norm with frozen running stats, relu, add_) in fixed 8-sample chunks and copy each chunk result into one preallocated full-size output, eliminating the simultaneous full-resolution 25.69 MB temporaries. stages.2/stages.3 are deliberately outside the boundary: their eager moments (max ~104-111 MB at (32,256,14,14)) already sit below the post-edit floor set by the chunked stages.0 moment (~137 MB) and the installed stem moment (~116 MB), so replacing them would add eliminated-call surface and launch overhead without moving the objective. Mixed groups (c1271430eda49ac23557 BasicLayer, 674c5372332029095322 Sequential, 867f8d20e37fedce71c4 ResNetConvLayer, 798df708d05932b17f71 profiler-exit markers) are not selected because they also contain stages.2 calls this proposal does not touch; their in-region member calls remain in affected_calls as eliminated observations. No functional replacements are installed, so no global dispatch overhead is added (legacy binding backend, direct callable boundaries), and the installed chunked-stem replacement composes unchanged: it returns one contiguous (32,64,56,56) fp32 tensor exactly as the parent embedder did (verified in the current trace: embedder call fa7ef6548e3a2d54174caeba emits count=4 batch-8 chunk reference calls).
hypothesis: Chunking stages.0 and stages.1 at their module boundaries in fixed 8-sample chunks (4 chunks for the frozen batch 32; remainder loop for other batch sizes) drops the peak moment from 5 simultaneous 25,690,112 B (32,64,56,56) activations plus resident weights/pixels to: weights 46,758,048 + pixels 19,267,584 + full stem output 25,690,112 (chunked input) + preallocated (32,64,56,56) stage-0 output 25,690,112 + <=3 concurrent 6,422,528 B (8,64,56,56) chunk temporaries ~ 136.7 MB plus small batch-8 conv workspace, with the stages.1 chunk moment (~120.6 MB: 25.69 MB input + 12,845,056 B prealloc + <=5 x 3,211,264 B chunk temporaries), the unedited stages.2 moment (~111 MB) and the stem moment (~116 MB) all below it. Expected peak_allocated_bytes ~140-150 MB versus the accepted 204,905,472 (-27% to -32%; ~-47% to -50% versus the original 281,975,808), to be measured by the paired evaluator. Throughput floor images_per_second >= 7120.31 (latency <= 4.4942 ms): current accepted latency 4.034 ms leaves ~460 us headroom; the edit adds ~38.5 MB of contiguous D2D chunk copies (~45 us at the ~900 GB/s effective bandwidth observed in the diagnostic trace) and ~100 extra host launches, which the previously observed ~2 ms host dispatch slack absorbs; the accepted stem candidate already demonstrated batch-8 chunked cudnn convs measure no throughput loss (7824-7986 ips vs 7495 baseline). Quality: conv2d, eval-mode batch_norm (training=False, frozen running stats), relu, add_ and the 1x1 stride-2 shortcut conv are strictly per-sample, so fixed-batch chunking is elementwise exact; logits expected within atol=rtol=1e-4 with exact top-1 and the +1-corruption control still rejected, verified by the frozen evaluator's repeated-forward closeness and top-1 checks in observe(). Risks left to measurement: cudnn algorithm choice at batch-8 chunk shapes for 3x3/1x1 convs at 56x56/28x28 (round-off ~1e-6 relative at worst, far below 1e-4 tolerance) and chunk-copy bandwidth; chunk size remains retunable inside the same boundary without changing the selection.
